web_evidence.note: The publisher-authorized opening sustains third-person narration of Mark, Ricky, and their family, including Mark's feelings and history, with no participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: John Grisham Writing Styles in The Client
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies the novel's narration as third person and explains that the unobtrusive narrator enters the minds of multiple characters.

web_evidence.title: The Client Part 1, Chapters 1-11 Summary & Analysis

web_evidence.title: The Client Part 2, Chapters 12-21 Summary & Analysis

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person, with access to multiple characters' thoughts. The strongest quote passages narrate sustained scenes around Mark and Dianne in third person, while all visible I/you counterexamples are dialogue or generic maxims. The authorized opening, a whole-book POV description, and analyses of both early and interior chapters agree, and no evidence of an autonomous first- or second-person section was found. The only limitation is that the Tier A prose source covers the opening rather than the entire novel; the later Goodreads passages and explicit structural sources supply the broader corroboration.
